selection.explanation: All three candidates pass the basic tests, but they differ in correctness against the full ISO 8601 spec. The critical difference is in fraction validation. According to ISO 8601, only the final component of the entire duration expression can have a fractional part. n2 correctly implements this by collecting all components (both date and time) into a single list and validating that if any component has a fraction, it must be the last one in the combined list. n1 and n4 (which are identical) validate fractions only within each section—date components separately from time components—which would incorrectly allow "P1.5YT2H" (fraction on the last date component even though time components follow). This is a subtle but significant correctness issue since the incomplete test suite doesn't catch this edge case. n2 also uses regex-based parsing which is cleaner and more maintainable than the manual character-by-character parsing in n1/n4. Both approaches handle the core requirements adequately when the edge case isn't present, and n1/n4's use of the calendar module for day clamping is marginally cleaner than n2's manual calculation, but correctness takes priority over such minor implementation differences.
